q: Energy resources are all forms of fuel used in the modern world, either for heating, ____ of electrical energy, or for other forms of energy conversion processes.
e: Energy resources are all forms of fuel used in the modern world, either for heating, generation of electrical energy, or for other forms of energy conversion processes. Generation here means producing electrical energy from a fuel or flow.

q: Renewable energy sources (____ energy sources) do not pollute the environment and natural surrounding and require less expenditure.
e: Renewable energy sources (non-conventional energy sources) do not pollute the environment and natural surrounding and require less expenditure. Renewable, or non-conventional, sources are replenished by natural processes on a human time scale.

q: Energy demand is the term used to describe the ____ of energy by human activities.
e: Energy demand is the term used to describe the consumption of energy by human activities. Energy demand is the energy people actually consume, shaped by population, industry and technology.

q: Energy demand depends on different ____ factors such as population, urbanization, industrialization, net capital income and development of technologies, etc.
e: Energy demand depends on different socioeconomic factors such as population, urbanization, industrialization, net capital income and development of technologies, etc. Energy demand is the energy people actually consume, shaped by population, industry and technology.

q: Energy demand ____ is crucial for ensuring future economic growth and environmental security.
e: Energy demand forecasting is crucial for ensuring future economic growth and environmental security. Energy demand is the energy people actually consume, shaped by population, industry and technology.

q: The energy crisis is the concern that the world's demands on the limited natural resources that are used to power industrial society are ____ as the demand rises.
e: The energy crisis is the concern that the world's demands on the limited natural resources that are used to power industrial society are diminishing as the demand rises. An energy crisis is a disruption of supply that threatens the economy and national security as demand keeps rising.

q: With ____ percent of the world's oil reserves already discovered, people need to find new ways to make energy.
e: With ninety percent of the world's oil reserves already discovered, people need to find new ways to make energy. ninety is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Since the ____ resources of the energy will not last long and cannot be regained, the world is going to face the problem of energy crisis in near future.
e: Since the non-renewable resources of the energy will not last long and cannot be regained, the world is going to face the problem of energy crisis in near future. A non-renewable source is not replenished as fast as we use it.

q: At present day, the rate of formation of fossil fuels (coal, petroleum, natural gas) is estimated to be about ____ and the world's consumption of energy is of the order of $10^{17}$ Btu/year.
e: At present day, the rate of formation of fossil fuels (coal, petroleum, natural gas) is estimated to be about 4 × 10⁹ kW and the world's consumption of energy is of the order of 10¹⁷ Btu/year. Coal, oil and natural gas are fossil fuels: non-renewable stores that form far slower than we burn them.

q: Today's world consumption of energy is of the order of ____.
e: Today's world consumption of energy is of the order of 10¹⁷ Btu/year. 10¹⁷ Btu/year is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Using 1 Btu = ____ and 1 year = $3.15 \times 10^7 \text{ s}$.
e: Using 1 Btu = 1055 J and 1 year = 3.15 × 10⁷ s. 1055 J is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: In our daily life we use different forms of energy such as heat energy, light energy, mechanical energy, electrical energy, chemical energy and ____ energy.
e: In our daily life we use different forms of energy such as heat energy, light energy, mechanical energy, electrical energy, chemical energy and sound energy. sound is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: A non-renewable resource is a natural substance that is not ____ with the speed at which it is consumed.
e: A non-renewable resource is a natural substance that is not replenished with the speed at which it is consumed. A non-renewable source is not replenished as fast as we use it.

q: Non-renewable energy resources include coal, natural gas, crude oil, and ____ energy.
e: Non-renewable energy resources include coal, natural gas, crude oil, and nuclear energy. Nuclear fission consumes uranium fuel, so that source is classed as non-renewable.

q: Renewable energy sources (also called non-conventional energy sources) are ____ replenished by natural processes.
e: Renewable energy sources (also called non-conventional energy sources) are continuously replenished by natural processes. Renewable, or non-conventional, sources are replenished by natural processes on a human time scale.

q: Renewable resources are replenished naturally and over short periods of time, so are in a virtually ____ supply.
e: Renewable resources are replenished naturally and over short periods of time, so are in a virtually unlimited supply. Renewable, or non-conventional, sources are replenished by natural processes on a human time scale.

q: Fossil fuels, such as coal, oil and natural gas, are important ____ sources of energy.
e: Fossil fuels, such as coal, oil and natural gas, are important non-renewable sources of energy. A non-renewable source is not replenished as fast as we use it.

q: ____ is the main constituent of these fossil fuels.
e: Carbon is the main constituent of these fossil fuels. Coal, oil and natural gas are fossil fuels: non-renewable stores that form far slower than we burn them.

q: A large amount of ____ energy is stored in the fossil fuels.
e: A large amount of chemical energy is stored in the fossil fuels. Coal, oil and natural gas are fossil fuels: non-renewable stores that form far slower than we burn them.

q: Fossil fuels are excellent sources of energy for our ____ needs.
e: Fossil fuels are excellent sources of energy for our transportation needs. Coal, oil and natural gas are fossil fuels: non-renewable stores that form far slower than we burn them.

q: Fossil fuel liquids also are refined into ____ products that are used as ingredients in the manufacture of literally hundreds of products from plastics and polyurethane to solvents.
e: Fossil fuel liquids also are refined into petrochemical products that are used as ingredients in the manufacture of literally hundreds of products from plastics and polyurethane to solvents. Coal, oil and natural gas are fossil fuels: non-renewable stores that form far slower than we burn them.

q: Coal is formed in a way similar to the other fossil fuels, though it goes through a different process called ____.
e: Coal is formed in a way similar to the other fossil fuels, though it goes through a different process called coalification. Coal, oil and natural gas are fossil fuels: non-renewable stores that form far slower than we burn them.

q: ____ is another major source of the energy in our country.
e: Natural gas is another major source of the energy in our country. A gas has no fixed volume; p, V and T follow Boyle and Charles.

q: Methane is a common gas found in swamps and is also the by-product of animals' ____ system.
e: Methane is a common gas found in swamps and is also the by-product of animals' digestive system. Methane is a swamp gas and a digestive by-product; it is also the main component of natural gas.

q: Nuclear energy is non-renewable as the uranium fuels used are consumed in the nuclear ____ reaction and hence are non-replenishable.
e: Nuclear energy is non-renewable as the uranium fuels used are consumed in the nuclear fission reaction and hence are non-replenishable. Nuclear fission consumes uranium fuel, so that source is classed as non-renewable.

q: Nevertheless, nuclear energy has many uses: energy produced in a nuclear ____ can be harnessed to produce electricity.
e: Nevertheless, nuclear energy has many uses: energy produced in a nuclear reactor can be harnessed to produce electricity. Nuclear fission consumes uranium fuel, so that source is classed as non-renewable.

q: Nuclear energy is also being used to power ____ and ship.
e: Nuclear energy is also being used to power submarines and ship. Nuclear fission consumes uranium fuel, so that source is classed as non-renewable.

q: ____ obtained as by-products in nuclear reactions are used in medicine, agriculture and research.
e: Radioisotopes obtained as by-products in nuclear reactions are used in medicine, agriculture and research. Nuclear fission consumes uranium fuel, so that source is classed as non-renewable.

q: The major types of renewable energy sources are: (i) solar, (ii) wind, (iii) hydropower, (iv) ocean, (v) geothermal and (vi) ____.
e: The major types of renewable energy sources are: (i) solar, (ii) wind, (iii) hydropower, (iv) ocean, (v) geothermal and (vi) biomass. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals.

q: Sun is one of the most ____ renewable sources of energy.
e: Sun is one of the most powerful renewable sources of energy. Renewable, or non-conventional, sources are replenished by natural processes on a human time scale.

q: Earth's atmosphere and clouds absorb or scatter as much as ____ of the incoming sunlight.
e: Earth's atmosphere and clouds absorb or scatter as much as 54% of the incoming sunlight. 54% is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The sunlight that reaches the ground consists of visible light, infrared, ultraviolet and other forms of ____ radiation.
e: The sunlight that reaches the ground consists of visible light, infrared, ultraviolet and other forms of electromagnetic radiation. electromagnetic is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The total amount of radiation energy passing through per unit area and per unit time is called ____ and is measured in W $m^{-2}$ or kW $m^{-2}$.
e: The total amount of radiation energy passing through per unit area and per unit time is called irradiance and is measured in W m⁻² or kW m⁻². Solar energy is the Sun's radiant light and heat. Irradiance is that radiation per unit area per unit time.

q: Another commonly used term for irradiance of sunlight is ____.
e: Another commonly used term for irradiance of sunlight is insolation. Solar energy is the Sun's radiant light and heat. Irradiance is that radiation per unit area per unit time.

q: Insolation is the solar irradiance received on a ____ surface such as the ground.
e: Insolation is the solar irradiance received on a horizontal surface such as the ground. The horizontal part of N or lift is the centripetal component on a banked path.

q: Above the earth's atmosphere, solar radiation has an intensity of approximately ____.
e: Above the earth's atmosphere, solar radiation has an intensity of approximately 1350 W m⁻². 1350 W m⁻² is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: At the earth's surface solar radiation has an intensity of approximately ____ on a clear day at solar noon in the summer months.
e: At the earth's surface solar radiation has an intensity of approximately 1000 W m⁻² on a clear day at solar noon in the summer months. 1000 W m⁻² is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Conversion of light energy into electrical energy is based on a phenomenon called ____ effect.
e: Conversion of light energy into electrical energy is based on a phenomenon called photovoltaic effect. The photovoltaic effect turns light into electrical energy inside a semiconductor junction.

q: When ____ materials are exposed to light, some of the photons of light are absorbed by the crystal which causes a significant number of free electrons in the crystal.
e: When semiconductor materials are exposed to light, some of the photons of light are absorbed by the crystal which causes a significant number of free electrons in the crystal. semiconductor is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: A solar cell is basically a ____ diode.
e: A solar cell is basically a p-n junction diode. A solar cell converts light to electricity; panels are modules made by combining cells.

q: The light energy, in the form of photons, supplies sufficient energy to the junction to create a number of ____ pairs.
e: The light energy, in the form of photons, supplies sufficient energy to the junction to create a number of electron-hole pairs. electron-hole is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Individual solar cells can be combined to form ____ commonly known as solar panels.
e: Individual solar cells can be combined to form modules commonly known as solar panels. A solar cell converts light to electricity; panels are modules made by combining cells.

q: Achieving the perfect ____ sun rays is the optimal orientation so that solar panels receive direct light throughout the day.
e: Achieving the perfect perpendicular sun rays is the optimal orientation so that solar panels receive direct light throughout the day. Perpendicular means the two directions stand at right angles.

q: Power conversion ____ of the solar panel is the ratio of the electrical power delivered by the panel to the solar power received by it.
e: Power conversion efficiency of the solar panel is the ratio of the electrical power delivered by the panel to the solar power received by it. A solar cell converts light to electricity; panels are modules made by combining cells.

q: Solar water heating systems installed in homes are comprised of three main elements: the solar ____, insulated piping, and a hot water storage tank.
e: Solar water heating systems installed in homes are comprised of three main elements: the solar collector, insulated piping, and a hot water storage tank. collector is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The solar collector gathers the heat from solar ____ and transfers the heat to water.
e: The solar collector gathers the heat from solar radiation and transfers the heat to water. radiation is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: ____ collectors are the most common type of collector.
e: Flat plate collectors are the most common type of collector. Flat-plate collectors are the ordinary panels used for solar heating.

q: Flat plate collectors have copper pipes attached to an ____ plate contained in an insulated box that is covered with a tempered glass or polymer cover plate.
e: Flat plate collectors have copper pipes attached to an absorber plate contained in an insulated box that is covered with a tempered glass or polymer cover plate. absorber is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Concentrated solar power (CSP) systems generate solar power by using ____ or lenses to concentrate a large area of sunlight onto a specific point of receiver which converts into heat.
e: Concentrated solar power (CSP) systems generate solar power by using mirrors or lenses to concentrate a large area of sunlight onto a specific point of receiver which converts into heat. mirrors is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The heat is then used to create ____, which drives a turbine to generate electrical power.
e: The heat is then used to create steam, which drives a turbine to generate electrical power. Heat raises steam, and that steam turns a turbine to make electricity.

q: Therefore CSP plants consist of two parts: one that collects solar energy and converts it to heat, and another that converts the heat energy to ____.
e: Therefore CSP plants consist of two parts: one that collects solar energy and converts it to heat, and another that converts the heat energy to electricity. Solar energy is the Sun's radiant light and heat. Irradiance is that radiation per unit area per unit time.

q: There are four types of CSP technologies: (a) ____ systems, (b) Linear fresnel systems, (c) Power tower systems and (d) Parabolic dish systems.
e: There are four types of CSP technologies: (a) Parabolic trough systems, (b) Linear fresnel systems, (c) Power tower systems and (d) Parabolic dish systems. A parabolic trough is one of the four CSP concentrator families.

q: Wind energy is the energy generated or produced by ____ the power of the wind.
e: Wind energy is the energy generated or produced by harnessing the power of the wind. Wind power incident on area A is P = ½ρAv³, so it grows with the cube of wind speed.

q: Both ____ and wind turbines harness wind energy and put it to practical use.
e: Both windmills and wind turbines harness wind energy and put it to practical use. Wind power incident on area A is P = ½ρAv³, so it grows with the cube of wind speed.

q: A wind turbine converts wind energy into electricity, which can then be used to power electrical equipment, stored in ____ or transmitted over power lines.
e: A wind turbine converts wind energy into electricity, which can then be used to power electrical equipment, stored in batteries or transmitted over power lines. Wind power incident on area A is P = ½ρAv³, so it grows with the cube of wind speed.

q: In a wind turbine, wind first hits the ____ of the turbine, causing them to rotate and turn the turbine connected to them.
e: In a wind turbine, wind first hits the blades of the turbine, causing them to rotate and turn the turbine connected to them. blades is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Wind farms consist of many individual wind turbines, which are connected to the electric power ____ network.
e: Wind farms consist of many individual wind turbines, which are connected to the electric power transmission network. transmission is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The amount of power that can be harvested from wind depends on the size of the turbine and the ____ of its blades.
e: The amount of power that can be harvested from wind depends on the size of the turbine and the length of its blades. length is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Wind energy is the ____ energy of air in motion.
e: Wind energy is the kinetic energy of air in motion. Wind power incident on area A is P = ½ρAv³, so it grows with the cube of wind speed.

q: Theoretically, when wind speed doubles, wind power potential increases by a factor of ____.
e: Theoretically, when wind speed doubles, wind power potential increases by a factor of eight. Because P ∝ v³, doubling v multiplies power by 2³ = 8.

q: Wind turbines, like windmills, are mounted on a ____ to capture the most energy.
e: Wind turbines, like windmills, are mounted on a tower to capture the most energy. tower is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The flowing water and water stored in huge ____ is also a very important source of energy which is known as hydroelectric energy.
e: The flowing water and water stored in huge dams is also a very important source of energy which is known as hydroelectric energy. Hydroelectric plants turn gravitational potential energy of water into kinetic energy and then electrical energy.

q: Hydropower, or hydroelectric power, is one of the oldest and ____ sources of renewable energy.
e: Hydropower, or hydroelectric power, is one of the oldest and largest sources of renewable energy. Hydroelectric plants turn gravitational potential energy of water into kinetic energy and then electrical energy.

q: There are three types of hydropower facilities: ____, diversion, and pumped storage.
e: There are three types of hydropower facilities: impoundment, diversion, and pumped storage. impoundment is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The most common type of hydroelectric power plant is an ____ facility.
e: The most common type of hydroelectric power plant is an impoundment facility. Hydroelectric plants turn gravitational potential energy of water into kinetic energy and then electrical energy.

q: Water is collected or stored at a higher elevation and gravity pulls the water downward through large pipes or tunnels (____) to a lower elevation.
e: Water is collected or stored at a higher elevation and gravity pulls the water downward through large pipes or tunnels (penstocks) to a lower elevation. penstocks is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The difference in these two elevations is known as the ____.
e: The difference in these two elevations is known as the head. Head is the elevation difference that sets the gravitational potential of the water.

q: At the end of its passage down the pipes, the falling water causes turbines to ____.
e: At the end of its passage down the pipes, the falling water causes turbines to rotate. rotate is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The turbines in turn drive generators, which convert ____ energy into electricity.
e: The turbines in turn drive generators, which convert mechanical energy into electricity. mechanical is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Transformers are then used to convert the ____ voltage of the generators to a higher voltage suitable for long-distance transmission.
e: Transformers are then used to convert the alternating voltage of the generators to a higher voltage suitable for long-distance transmission. alternating is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: A penstock is a closed ____ that channels the flow of water to turbines with water flow regulated by gates and valves.
e: A penstock is a closed conduit that channels the flow of water to turbines with water flow regulated by gates and valves. conduit is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: A diversion, sometimes called a ____ facility, channels a portion of a river through a canal or a penstock to utilize the natural decline of the river bed elevation to produce energy.
e: A diversion, sometimes called a run-of-river facility, channels a portion of a river through a canal or a penstock to utilize the natural decline of the river bed elevation to produce energy. run-of-river is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Another type of hydropower is ____ hydropower (PSH).
e: Another type of hydropower is pumped storage hydropower (PSH). pumped storage is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: A PSH facility is able to ____ the electricity generated by other power sources.
e: A PSH facility is able to store the electricity generated by other power sources. store is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: When the demand for electricity is low, a PSH facility stores energy by pumping water from the lower reservoir to an ____ reservoir at a higher elevation.
e: When the demand for electricity is low, a PSH facility stores energy by pumping water from the lower reservoir to an upper reservoir at a higher elevation. upper is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: During periods of high electrical ____, the water is released back to the lower reservoir and turns a turbine, generating electricity.
e: During periods of high electrical demand, the water is released back to the lower reservoir and turns a turbine, generating electricity. demand is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The power available from falling water can be calculated from the flow rate and ____ of water, the height of fall, and the local acceleration due to gravity.
e: The power available from falling water can be calculated from the flow rate and density of water, the height of fall, and the local acceleration due to gravity. density is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Due to the gravitational pull of mainly the ____ on the spinning earth, the level of water in the sea rises and falls.
e: Due to the gravitational pull of mainly the moon on the spinning earth, the level of water in the sea rises and falls. moon is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The tidal energy is produced by the ____ in sea levels.
e: The tidal energy is produced by the difference in sea levels. difference is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: A tidal barrage works similarly to a large hydropower reservoir dam but it is placed at the entrance to a bay or ____.
e: A tidal barrage works similarly to a large hydropower reservoir dam but it is placed at the entrance to a bay or estuary. estuary is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The kinetic energy of huge waves near the ____ can be trapped to generate electricity.
e: The kinetic energy of huge waves near the seashore can be trapped to generate electricity. seashore is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The waves are generated by strong ____ blowing across the sea.
e: The waves are generated by strong winds blowing across the sea. winds is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The water at the surface of the sea or ocean is heated by the sun while the water in deeper sections is relatively ____.
e: The water at the surface of the sea or ocean is heated by the sun while the water in deeper sections is relatively cold. cold is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The warm surface-water is used to boil a volatile liquid (e.g. ____, boiling point ~ $-33.34^\circ\text{C}$).
e: The warm surface-water is used to boil a volatile liquid (e.g. ammonia, boiling point ~ -33.34^circC). ammonia is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The ____ of the liquid (ammonia) are then used to run the turbine of generator.
e: The vapours of the liquid (ammonia) are then used to run the turbine of generator. vapours is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The cold water from the depth of the ocean is pumped up and ____ vapour again to liquid.
e: The cold water from the depth of the ocean is pumped up and condense vapour again to liquid. condense is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Geothermal energy is a type of renewable energy taken from the Earth's ____ (the internal heat of the earth) and it is one of the oldest types of natural sources of heat.
e: Geothermal energy is a type of renewable energy taken from the Earth's core (the internal heat of the earth) and it is one of the oldest types of natural sources of heat. Geothermal energy is heat from the Earth's interior, used to drive turbines.

q: Thermal energy from ____ can be used to generate electricity.
e: Thermal energy from magma can be used to generate electricity. magma is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Magma is extremely hot liquid and ____ rock located under Earth's surface.
e: Magma is extremely hot liquid and semi-liquid rock located under Earth's surface. semi-liquid is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: ____ of up to a mile deep or more are drilled into underground reservoirs to tap into the geothermal resources.
e: Wells of up to a mile deep or more are drilled into underground reservoirs to tap into the geothermal resources. Geothermal energy is heat from the Earth's interior, used to drive turbines.

q: Cooled water is pumped into heated rocks where it is turned into ____, which then rises up to drive the turbines and generate electricity.
e: Cooled water is pumped into heated rocks where it is turned into steam, which then rises up to drive the turbines and generate electricity. Heat raises steam, and that steam turns a turbine to make electricity.

q: Biomass is renewable ____ material that comes from plants and animals.
e: Biomass is renewable organic material that comes from plants and animals. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals.

q: Biomass contains stored ____ energy.
e: Biomass contains stored chemical energy. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals.

q: Biomass sources for energy include: Wood and wood processing wastes, Agricultural crops and waste materials, Biogenic materials in municipal solid waste, Animal manure and human ____.
e: Biomass sources for energy include: Wood and wood processing wastes, Agricultural crops and waste materials, Biogenic materials in municipal solid waste, Animal manure and human sewage. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals.

q: Biomass is converted to energy through various processes, including: direct ____ (burning) to produce heat, thermochemical conversion, chemical conversion, biological conversion.
e: Biomass is converted to energy through various processes, including: direct combustion (burning) to produce heat, thermochemical conversion, chemical conversion, biological conversion. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals.

q: ____ combustion is the most common method for converting biomass to useful energy.
e: Direct combustion is the most common method for converting biomass to useful energy. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals.

q: Thermochemical conversion of biomass includes ____ and gasification.
e: Thermochemical conversion of biomass includes pyrolysis and gasification. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals.

q: Both are thermal decomposition processes in which biomass feedstock materials are heated in closed, pressurized vessels called ____ at high temperatures.
e: Both are thermal decomposition processes in which biomass feedstock materials are heated in closed, pressurized vessels called gasifiers at high temperatures. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals.

q: Biomass pyrolysis produces fuels such as ____, bio-oil, renewable diesel, methane, and hydrogen.
e: Biomass pyrolysis produces fuels such as charcoal, bio-oil, renewable diesel, methane, and hydrogen. Coal, oil and natural gas are fossil fuels: non-renewable stores that form far slower than we burn them.

q: Biomass gasification produces a carbon monoxide and hydrogen rich gas called synthesis gas or ____.
e: Biomass gasification produces a carbon monoxide and hydrogen rich gas called synthesis gas or syngas. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals.

q: Chemical conversion process known as ____ is used for converting vegetable oils, animal fats, and greases into biodiesel.
e: Chemical conversion process known as transesterification is used for converting vegetable oils, animal fats, and greases into biodiesel. transesterification is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Biological conversion includes ____ to convert biomass into ethanol and anaerobic digestion to produce natural gas.
e: Biological conversion includes fermentation to convert biomass into ethanol and anaerobic digestion to produce natural gas. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals.

q: Natural gas, also called ____ or biomethane, is produced in anaerobic digesters at sewage treatment plants and at dairy and livestock operations.
e: Natural gas, also called biogas or biomethane, is produced in anaerobic digesters at sewage treatment plants and at dairy and livestock operations. Coal, oil and natural gas are fossil fuels: non-renewable stores that form far slower than we burn them.

q: The environmental problems directly related to energy production and consumption include air pollution, climate change, water pollution, ____ pollution, and solid waste disposal.
e: The environmental problems directly related to energy production and consumption include air pollution, climate change, water pollution, thermal pollution, and solid waste disposal. thermal is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The problems that relate to the use of fossil fuels are: global warming, ____ rains, dangers posed by leaded fuels, oil spills, gas leaks and explosions.
e: The problems that relate to the use of fossil fuels are: global warming, acid rains, dangers posed by leaded fuels, oil spills, gas leaks and explosions. Coal, oil and natural gas are fossil fuels: non-renewable stores that form far slower than we burn them.

q: Global warming refers to the gradual increase in the average temperature of the earth's surface and its atmosphere which has been attributed to the ____ of greenhouse gases.
e: Global warming refers to the gradual increase in the average temperature of the earth's surface and its atmosphere which has been attributed to the accumulation of greenhouse gases. accumulation is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The main greenhouse gases are carbon dioxide, methane, water vapour, oxides of nitrogen and ____.
e: The main greenhouse gases are carbon dioxide, methane, water vapour, oxides of nitrogen and chlorofluorocarbons. Methane is a swamp gas and a digestive by-product; it is also the main component of natural gas.

q: CFCs also destroy the earth's protective ____ layer which shields the earth from harmful ultraviolet (UV) rays from the sun.
e: CFCs also destroy the earth's protective ozone layer which shields the earth from harmful ultraviolet (UV) rays from the sun. ozone is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Acid rains are caused mainly by the release of ____ dioxide and oxides of nitrogen when fossil fuels burn.
e: Acid rains are caused mainly by the release of sulphur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen when fossil fuels burn. Coal, oil and natural gas are fossil fuels: non-renewable stores that form far slower than we burn them.

q: The oxides combine with water ____ in the air to form acids, which return to the ground as acid rain.
e: The oxides combine with water vapour in the air to form acids, which return to the ground as acid rain. Acid rain forms when SO₂ and NOₓ mix with water and oxygen in the air to make acidic pollutants.

q: Because ____ acid is a relatively weak acid, the ability of carbon dioxide alone to generate true acid rain is very limited.
e: Because carbonic acid is a relatively weak acid, the ability of carbon dioxide alone to generate true acid rain is very limited. Acid rain forms when SO₂ and NOₓ mix with water and oxygen in the air to make acidic pollutants.

q: The problems posed by acid rains include ____ of the built environment, soil degradation, water pollution and depletion of forests.
e: The problems posed by acid rains include corrosion of the built environment, soil degradation, water pollution and depletion of forests. Acid rain forms when SO₂ and NOₓ mix with water and oxygen in the air to make acidic pollutants.

q: The oil industry adds ____ (Pb) to petrol (gasoline) to help engines run more smoothly.
e: The oil industry adds lead (Pb) to petrol (gasoline) to help engines run more smoothly. lead is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Vehicles that burn leaded gasoline pour out leaded ____ that contaminate the air.
e: Vehicles that burn leaded gasoline pour out leaded fumes that contaminate the air. fumes is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The World Health Organisation (WHO) has established that smoke from the combustion of leaded fuels in vehicles causes ____ and high blood pressure in adults.
e: The World Health Organisation (WHO) has established that smoke from the combustion of leaded fuels in vehicles causes cancer and high blood pressure in adults. cancer is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: In children, it impairs mental development, reduces intelligence thus hindering learning ability and causes ____ disorders.
e: In children, it impairs mental development, reduces intelligence thus hindering learning ability and causes behavioural disorders. behavioural is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Oil spills seriously damage the land, ____, and water bodies, including the oceans.
e: Oil spills seriously damage the land, vegetation, and water bodies, including the oceans. vegetation is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Excavated areas that have been strip mined for coal but are not filled and revegetated cause water pollution as surface water runoff from the mined area can flush ____ and sulphur-bearing compounds into nearby streams and rivers.
e: The blank is sediments. Coal, oil and natural gas are fossil fuels: non-renewable stores that form far slower than we burn them. That word is the one that completes the idea about Excavated areas been strip mined coal.

q: Emissions from vehicles, thermal power plants and factories contain unburned ____, particulates, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and oxides of nitrogen and sulphur that contribute to the lowering of the quality of air.
e: The blank is hydrocarbons. That word is the one that completes the idea about Emissions vehicles thermal power plants factories.

q: Over its estimated life a photovoltaic module will produce much more electricity than was used in its ____.
e: Over its estimated life a photovoltaic module will produce much more electricity than was used in its production. The photovoltaic effect turns light into electrical energy inside a semiconductor junction.

q: A solar module will prevent the emission of ____ produced by other conventional energy sources.
e: A solar module will prevent the emission of CO₂ produced by other conventional energy sources. CO₂ is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: PV cell technologies have relatively lower environmental ____ compared to other types of electric sources.
e: PV cell technologies have relatively lower environmental risks compared to other types of electric sources. risks is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: A wind farm, when installed on ____ land, has one of the lowest environmental impacts of all energy sources.
e: A wind farm, when installed on agricultural land, has one of the lowest environmental impacts of all energy sources. agricultural is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Modern wind turbine designs have significantly reduced the ____ from turbines.
e: Modern wind turbine designs have significantly reduced the noise from turbines. Blade and gearbox design have cut the sound from modern wind turbines.

q: Low frequency sound and ____ (i.e. usually beneath the threshold of human hearing) are everywhere in the environment.
e: Low frequency sound and infrasound (i.e. usually beneath the threshold of human hearing) are everywhere in the environment. infrasound is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Wind turbines may create shadow ____ on nearby residences when the sun passes behind the turbine.
e: Wind turbines may create shadow flicker on nearby residences when the sun passes behind the turbine. flicker is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Although hydropower has no air quality impacts, construction and operation of hydropower dams can significantly affect natural ____ systems as well as fish and wildlife populations.
e: Although hydropower has no air quality impacts, construction and operation of hydropower dams can significantly affect natural river systems as well as fish and wildlife populations. river is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: In flat basins large dams cause ____ of large tracts of land, destroying local animals and habitats.
e: In flat basins large dams cause flooding of large tracts of land, destroying local animals and habitats. flooding is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Villages and people have to be ____ causing change in life style.
e: Villages and people have to be displaced causing change in life style. displaced is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Large amounts of plant life are submerged and decay ____.
e: Large amounts of plant life are submerged and decay anaerobically. anaerobically is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Dams restrict ____ that are responsible for the fertile lands downstream.
e: Dams restrict sediments that are responsible for the fertile lands downstream. sediments is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Large dams are breeding grounds for ____ and cause the spread of disease.
e: Large dams are breeding grounds for mosquitoes and cause the spread of disease. mosquitoes is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Dams serve as a heat ____, water in dams is hotter than the normal river water and when this warm water released into the river downstream can affect animal life.
e: Dams serve as a heat sink, water in dams is hotter than the normal river water and when this warm water released into the river downstream can affect animal life. sink is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Geothermal power is a relatively ____ (less harmful) source of energy.
e: Geothermal power is a relatively benign (less harmful) source of energy. Geothermal energy is heat from the Earth's interior, used to drive turbines.

q: Worldwide geothermal energy utilization increases yearly because it is an attractive ____ to burning fossil fuels.
e: Worldwide geothermal energy utilization increases yearly because it is an attractive alternative to burning fossil fuels. Geothermal energy is heat from the Earth's interior, used to drive turbines.

q: Electricity generation from geothermal resources involves much lower greenhouse gas ____ rates than that from fossil fuels.
e: Electricity generation from geothermal resources involves much lower greenhouse gas emission rates than that from fossil fuels. Geothermal energy is heat from the Earth's interior, used to drive turbines.

q: Any large-scale construction and ____ operation will produce visual impacts on the landscape, create noise and wastes and affect local economy.
e: Any large-scale construction and drilling operation will produce visual impacts on the landscape, create noise and wastes and affect local economy. drilling is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Biomass power plants share some similarities with fossil fuel power plants: both involve the combustion of a ____ to generate electricity.
e: Biomass power plants share some similarities with fossil fuel power plants: both involve the combustion of a feedstock to generate electricity. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals.

q: Biomass power plants, like coal and natural gas-fired power plants, require water for ____.
e: Biomass power plants, like coal and natural gas-fired power plants, require water for cooling. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals.

q: Land use impacts from biomass power production are driven primarily by the type of feedstock: either a waste stream or an energy ____ that is grown specifically for generating electricity.
e: Land use impacts from biomass power production are driven primarily by the type of feedstock: either a waste stream or an energy crop that is grown specifically for generating electricity. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals.

q: There are global warming emissions associated with growing and ____ biomass feedstock, transporting feedstock to the power plant, and burning or gasifying the feedstock.
e: There are global warming emissions associated with growing and harvesting biomass feedstock, transporting feedstock to the power plant, and burning or gasifying the feedstock. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals.
